question: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha is a classic example of which style of temple architecture?
option_2: Kalinga style (a form of the Nagara school)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalinga style (a form of the Nagara school).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Konark Sun Temple is a masterpiece of the Kalinga style of temple architecture, which is the regional variant of the North Indian Nagara style developed in Odisha. (कलिंग शैली — कोणार्क)

 

• It was built in the 13th century CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty and is designed as a colossal chariot of the Sun God with 24 carved wheels and seven horses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The main parts of a Kalinga temple are the 'deul' (sanctum tower), the 'jagamohana' (assembly hall), the 'natamandira' (dance hall) and the 'bhoga-mandapa' (hall of offerings).

 

• Other famous Kalinga-style temples include the Lingaraja Temple and the Jagannath Temple (Puri) in Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• The Dravida style, with its towering gopurams, is characteristic of South Indian temples.

 

• The Vesara style is a hybrid of the Nagara and Dravida styles, seen in Karnataka.

question: Sarhul, a spring festival marked by the worship of nature and the sal tree, is a major festival of the tribal communities of which region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarhul is one of the most important festivals of the tribal (Adivasi) communities of Jharkhand and surrounding areas of eastern India. (सरहुल — झारखंड)

 

• Celebrated in spring, it marks the worship of nature, particularly the sal tree, and the village deity. It is associated with the beginning of the new year and the sowing season for the tribes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known tribal festivals of the Jharkhand region include Karam, Sohrai, Tusu and Jawa.

 

• The major tribes of Jharkhand include the Santhal, Munda, Oraon and Ho.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarhul is not a festival of Kerala, Punjab or Gujarat; it is specifically linked to the tribal culture of the Chhotanagpur plateau region.

question: The Manganiyar and Langa communities of Rajasthan are traditionally renowned for which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hereditary folk music and singing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Manganiyar and Langa are hereditary communities of professional folk musicians and singers from the desert regions of western Rajasthan (Jaisalmer, Barmer). (मांगणियार एवं लंगा — लोक संगीत)

 

• They have preserved a rich oral tradition of folk songs performed at births, weddings and other celebrations, using instruments such as the kamaicha, sarangi, dholak and khartal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthani folk music is closely tied to daily life, nature and folk tales, and is distinct from formal classical (raga-based) music.

 

• The kamaicha is a bowed string instrument especially associated with the Manganiyars.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan is also famous for miniature painting, blue pottery (Jaipur) and Kathputli (string puppetry), but these are not the specialities of the Manganiyar and Langa communities.

question: In the game of basketball, moving with the ball without dribbling it, by taking more than the permitted number of steps, is a violation known as which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Travelling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In basketball, 'travelling' is a violation that occurs when a player holding the ball moves one or both feet illegally — that is, takes too many steps without dribbling (bouncing) the ball. (ट्रैवलिंग — बास्केटबॉल)

 

• When a travelling violation is called, possession of the ball is awarded to the opposing team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 in the USA. A standard team has five players on the court.

 

NOTE

 

• A 'double dribble' occurs when a player dribbles, stops, and then dribbles again, or dribbles with both hands.

 

• 'Blocking' is an illegal personal contact foul that impedes an opponent's movement.

 

• A 'shot clock violation' occurs when a team fails to attempt a shot within the allotted time (e.g., 24 seconds).

question: The Regulating Act of 1773 created, for the first time, the office of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor-General of Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first major step taken by the British Parliament to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट, 1773)

 

• It created the office of the 'Governor-General of Bengal' and made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal. Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal.

 

• It also provided for a Council of four members to assist the Governor-General and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (Fort William) in 1774.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the 'Governor-General of India'; Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1858 created the office of 'Secretary of State for India' and the title 'Viceroy' (the first Viceroy was Lord Canning).

 

NOTE

 

• Pitt's India Act of 1784 established the Board of Control to supervise the civil and military affairs of the Company in India.

question: India won its first-ever Olympic gold medal as an independent nation at the 1948 London Olympics in which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first Olympic gold medal as an independent nation at the 1948 London Olympics in field hockey, defeating Great Britain in the final. (1948 लंदन ओलंपिक — हॉकी स्वर्ण)

 

• This victory was especially significant as it came soon after independence and was won on British soil against the host nation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian men's hockey team dominated the Olympics from 1928 to 1956, winning six consecutive gold medals. Legends such as Major Dhyan Chand were part of this golden era (before independence).

 

• India's first individual Olympic medal was won by K. D. Jadhav (bronze in wrestling, 1952 Helsinki).

 

NOTE

 

• India's very first Olympic medals overall were the two silver medals won by Norman Pritchard in athletics at the 1900 Paris Games, before independence.

question:
Match the following martial arts/combat sports with their country of origin:

1. Judo

2. Taekwondo

3. Kalaripayattu
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-Japan, 2-Korea, 3-India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: Judo - Japan; Taekwondo - Korea; Kalaripayattu - India. (मार्शल आर्ट एवं उनके उद्गम देश)

 

• Judo is a modern Japanese martial art founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882; it is an Olympic sport.

 

• Taekwondo is a Korean martial art known for its high, fast kicks; it is also an Olympic sport.

 

• Kalaripayattu is one of the oldest martial art forms in the world, originating in Kerala, India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other martial arts and their origins include Karate (Japan/Okinawa), Kung Fu (China) and Muay Thai (Thailand).

 

NOTE

 

• Kalaripayattu is often regarded as a forerunner of many Asian martial arts and is closely linked to the cultural heritage of Kerala.

question: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project aims to connect the ports of eastern India with which neighbouring country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects the Indian port of Kolkata with the Sittwe port in Myanmar by sea, and further links Sittwe to Mizoram in north-east India through the Kaladan river and road routes. (कलादान मल्टी-मॉडल परियोजना — म्यांमार)

 

• Its main aim is to provide an alternative connectivity route to India's landlocked north-eastern states, reducing dependence on the narrow 'Chicken's Neck' (Siliguri Corridor).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway is another major connectivity project linking India with Southeast Asia.

 

• Both projects support India's 'Act East' policy.

 

NOTE

 

• The project involves shipping, inland water transport and road transport, which is why it is called 'multi-modal'.

question: The autobiography 'Wings of Fire' was written by which of the following?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, co-written with Arun Tiwari. (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

 

• The book traces Kalam's early life and his contributions to India's space and missile programmes before he became the 11th President of India (2002-2007).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Kalam is popularly known as the 'Missile Man of India' for his role in developing India's ballistic missile and launch-vehicle technology.

 

• His other well-known books include 'Ignited Minds', 'India 2020' and 'The Turning Point'.

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme; Homi Bhabha as the father of India's nuclear programme; and C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for the 'Raman Effect'.

question: The Aga Khan Cup, one of the oldest tournaments in India, is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Aga Khan Cup is one of the oldest field hockey tournaments in India, first held in the early 20th century. (आगा खान कप — हॉकी)

 

• Hockey is often regarded as India's traditional strength, especially during its Olympic golden era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some important trophies associated with field hockey in India include the Aga Khan Cup, the Beighton Cup (Kolkata) and the Dhyan Chand Trophy.

 

• The Subroto Cup is associated with football, and the Santosh Trophy is the premier domestic football championship.

 

NOTE

 

• The Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy and Irani Trophy are associated with cricket; the Thomas Cup and Uber Cup are associated with badminton.

question: The 'Order of Zayed', the highest civilian honour of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), was conferred on which Indian leader in 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Order of Zayed', the highest civilian honour of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), was conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2019. (ऑर्डर ऑफ ज़ायेद — नरेंद्र मोदी)

 

• The award recognised his role in strengthening bilateral relations between India and the UAE. The honour is named after Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the founding father of the UAE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM Modi has received several other top foreign honours, including the 'Order of St. Andrew' (Russia), the 'King Hamad Order of the Renaissance' (Bahrain) and the 'Order of the Nile' (Egypt).

 

NOTE

 

• These are state honours conferred by foreign governments, distinct from India's own civilian awards such as the Bharat Ratna and the Padma awards.

question: The Chambal River is a major tributary of which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yamuna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chambal River is a major tributary of the Yamuna River. (चंबल — यमुना की सहायक नदी)

 

• The Chambal rises from the Janapav Hills in the Vindhyan range in Madhya Pradesh and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh before joining the Yamuna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chambal is known for its relatively unpolluted water and for the Gharial (a fish-eating crocodile) sanctuary at the National Chambal Sanctuary.

 

• Other tributaries of the Yamuna include the Betwa, Ken and Sindh rivers.

 

NOTE

 

• The Yamuna itself is the longest tributary of the Ganga; the Chambal is thus a sub-tributary of the Ganga system.

question: What was the name of the rover of India's Chandrayaan-3 mission that successfully explored the lunar surface in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pragyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The rover of the Chandrayaan-3 mission was named 'Pragyan' (meaning 'wisdom'), while the lander was named 'Vikram' (after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai). (प्रज्ञान — चंद्रयान-3 रोवर)

 

• Chandrayaan-3 made a successful soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to land near the south pole.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• To commemorate the landing, 23 August is now celebrated as 'National Space Day' in India.

 

• The landing site of Chandrayaan-3 has been named 'Shiv Shakti Point'.

 

NOTE

 

• Aryabhata was India's first satellite (1975); Bhaskara was an early Indian Earth-observation satellite. Vikram was the lander, not the rover, of Chandrayaan-3.

question: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulmonary vein.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated (oxygen-rich) blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. (फुफ्फुसीय शिरा — ऑक्सीजनयुक्त रक्त)

 

• It is one of the few veins in the body that carries oxygenated blood; most veins carry deoxygenated blood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pulmonary artery is one of the few arteries that carries deoxygenated blood — from the right ventricle to the lungs.

 

• The path of pulmonary circulation is: right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium.

 

NOTE

 

• The vena cava (superior and inferior) brings deoxygenated blood from the body into the right atrium.

 

• The aorta is the largest artery, carrying oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers in India:

Statement 1: Subjects of national importance, such as defence and foreign affairs, are included in the Union List.

Statement 2: In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a subject in the Concurrent List, the State law generally prevails.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only Statement 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Subjects of national importance, such as defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking and currency, are placed in the Union List, on which only Parliament can legislate. (संघ सूची)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union (Central) law generally prevails, not the State law (Article 254). The State law becomes void to the extent of the repugnancy.

 

• Hence, only Statement 1 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides powers into three lists: the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List.

 

• An exception to Statement 2: if a State law on a Concurrent subject is reserved for the President and receives assent, it can prevail in that State — but Parliament may still override it later.

 

NOTE

 

• The residuary powers (subjects not mentioned in any list) rest with the Union Parliament.

question: When a ray of light passes from air into a denser medium such as glass, which of the following properties of the light remains unchanged?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Its frequency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When light passes from one medium to another (for example, from air into glass), its frequency remains unchanged. (आवृत्ति अपरिवर्तित रहती है)

 

• The frequency of a wave is determined by its source and does not change when the wave enters a new medium. However, the speed and the wavelength of light do change, and the light usually bends (refracts), changing direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a denser medium, the speed of light decreases and its wavelength becomes shorter, but the frequency stays constant, keeping the colour of the light the same.

 

• The relationship is: speed = frequency × wavelength.

 

NOTE

 

• The same principle applies to sound waves: when sound travels from one medium to another, its frequency remains constant while its speed and wavelength change.

question: The provision for the organisation of village panchayats as units of self-government is included under which part of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The provision for the organisation of village panchayats is contained in Article 40, which is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). (राज्य नीति के निदेशक तत्व — ग्राम पंचायत)

 

• Article 40 directs the State to take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Directive Principles are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution and are inspired by the Irish Constitution. They are not enforceable by any court.

 

• Article 40 was later given effect through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• The concept of the Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) and the promotion of cottage industries (Article 43) are also part of the DPSP.

question: The tagline 'Har Ghar Jal' is associated with which of the following missions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jal Jeevan Mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The tagline 'Har Ghar Jal' (water to every household) is associated with the Jal Jeevan Mission. (हर घर जल — जल जीवन मिशन)

 

• Launched in 2019, the mission aims to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections (Functional Household Tap Connections) to all rural households.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jal Jeevan Mission is implemented under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

 

• The slogan 'Har Khet Ko Pani' (water to every field) is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), while 'Per Drop More Crop' promotes micro-irrigation.

 

NOTE

 

• The Swachh Bharat Mission focuses on sanitation; AMRUT on urban infrastructure; and Namami Gange on cleaning the river Ganga.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): Delhi experiences very severe air pollution, especially during the winter months.

Reason (R): During winter, temperature inversion traps pollutants close to the Earth's surface.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. Delhi records very high levels of air pollution, particularly in winter, when the Air Quality Index (AQI) often reaches the 'severe' category. (दिल्ली — शीतकालीन वायु प्रदूषण)

 

• Reason (R) is true. During winter, a temperature inversion often forms — a layer of warm air sits above a layer of cold air near the surface — which prevents the vertical mixing of air and traps pollutants close to the ground.

 

• R is the correct explanation of A: it is precisely because this inversion traps smoke, dust and vehicular/industrial emissions near the surface that pollution levels in Delhi become so severe in winter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other factors worsening Delhi's winter pollution include stubble (crop residue) burning in neighbouring states, low wind speeds and firecracker emissions.

 

NOTE

 

• A temperature inversion is a reversal of the normal situation in which temperature decreases with height.

question: Which of the following is the largest mangrove forest in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Sundarbans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sundarbans, located in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers in West Bengal (and Bangladesh), is the largest mangrove forest in India and the world. (सुंदरबन — मैंग्रोव वन)

 

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is famous as the natural habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger. The Sundarbans National Park is also a tiger reserve and biosphere reserve.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mangroves are salt-tolerant forests that grow in the intertidal zones of coasts and deltas and protect the coastline from erosion and cyclones.

 

• The name 'Sundarban' is often said to be derived from the 'Sundari' tree, which is common in the region.

 

NOTE

 

• The Gulf of Mannar is known for its coral reefs; the Western Ghats and the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve are biodiversity hotspots but are not mangrove forests.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): The Green Revolution in India led to a large increase in the production of pulses and oilseeds.

Reason (R): The Green Revolution was concentrated mainly on the crops wheat and rice.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is false. The Green Revolution did NOT lead to a large increase in the production of pulses and oilseeds. In fact, the production of pulses and oilseeds largely stagnated during this period. (हरित क्रांति)

 

• Reason (R) is true. The Green Revolution was concentrated mainly on the cereal crops wheat and rice, whose yields rose sharply with the use of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers and assured irrigation.

 

• Since the Assertion is false but the Reason is true, the correct option is "A is false, but R is true".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s and is associated with M. S. Swaminathan in India and Norman Borlaug internationally.

 

• Its benefits were also regionally uneven, being concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Efforts to raise pulse production later were addressed through initiatives such as the National Food Security Mission and calls for a 'second Green Revolution' and a 'Rainbow Revolution'.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Chhau dance:

Statement 1: It is a semi-classical dance with martial and folk traditions from Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

Statement 2: In its Purulia and Seraikella forms, performers wear elaborate masks.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial, tribal and folk origins. (छऊ नृत्य)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: It has three main styles named after their places of origin — Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The Purulia and Seraikella forms of Chhau are performed with elaborate masks, whereas the Mayurbhanj form is performed without masks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chhau dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

• The themes of Chhau are often drawn from the epics Ramayana and Mahabharata and from nature.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements about the Chhau dance are factually correct, so the answer is 'Both Statement 1 and Statement 2'.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to form new States and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form new States and to alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing States. (अनुच्छेद 3 — नए राज्यों का निर्माण)

 

• Such a Bill can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the President, and the President must first refer it to the concerned State Legislature for its views (though Parliament is not bound by those views).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States' and defines the territory of India.

 

• Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit or establish new States into the Union.

 

NOTE

 

• Because States can be reorganised by an ordinary law under Articles 2 and 3, India is often described as an 'indestructible Union of destructible States'.

question:
Consider the following statements about an Ordinance in India:

Statement 1: An Ordinance can be promulgated by the President when either House of Parliament is not in session.

Statement 2: An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. The ordinance-making power of the President is provided under Article 123 of the Constitution. (अध्यादेश — अनुच्छेद 123)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The President can promulgate an Ordinance when Parliament is not in session (i.e., when either House is not in session) and immediate action is required.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, but it is a temporary law.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• An Ordinance must be laid before both Houses of Parliament when they reassemble and ceases to operate six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, unless approved earlier.

 

• The Governor has a similar ordinance-making power at the State level under Article 213.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements about Ordinances are correct, so the answer is 'Both Statement 1 and Statement 2'.

question: In which layer of the Earth's atmosphere is the ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation, mainly found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stratosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, is mainly found in the stratosphere. (समताप मंडल — ओज़ोन परत)

 

• The stratosphere is the second layer of the atmosphere, lying above the troposphere. The absorption of UV rays by ozone causes the temperature to rise with height in the stratosphere, which makes this layer stable and ideal for jet aircraft to fly in.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The layers of the atmosphere, from the surface upwards, are: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere and Exosphere.

 

• The troposphere is where almost all weather phenomena occur.

 

NOTE

 

• In the thermosphere, temperature rises sharply due to the absorption of high-energy UV and X-ray radiation from the Sun; the mesosphere is the layer where most meteors burn up.
